mechanism: L-TF1: the first descent pass reuses the gradient the parent computed and checked before the loop instead of recomputing it. The in-loop recomputation is guarded with `if _pass:`. Nothing else changes.
parent: v230 Linear L-EM2 + v195 Attention complete root

sole_change_measured.method: build.py cuts the parent's own _em1_dynamic_descent source out of the parent bytes, substitutes one substring, and appends the result. It refuses to build unless that substring occurs exactly once in the unguarded form and zero times in the guarded form, and unless dissolving the inserted guard reproduces the parent's AST exactly.
sole_change_measured.edit: the four-line loop head `for / gradient = / if not isfinite / aborted` becomes `for / if _pass: / gradient = / if not isfinite / aborted` (the three following lines indent by four spaces)
sole_change_measured.why_not_a_differing_byte_count: this card inserts a line, so every byte after it shifts and a positional byte-by-byte comparison reports the whole tail as differing -- a large number that looks like evidence and is not. The two measures that do mean something are reported instead: the substring-substitution count, and the AST equality after the guard is dissolved.

shard_decision_note: the local tool's gate is `delta_mean > 0 and L1 < 0.02`, an eligibility screen for small local trends. Six zero shard means cannot pass it, and this archive does not claim a local pass. A zero here is the intended result, not a failed screen: the mechanism removes an operation whose result is discarded, so a non-zero gain delta would have been a defect.

timing_comparability_note: `api_total_seconds` is NOT comparable across these runs and is recorded only because the tool writes it. It includes hif4_calibration_and_quantize_weight, which is 128-143 s on a calibration-cache miss and 0.0 s on a hit: the candidate's shard-0 and shard-1 runs hit the cache and wrote 42.8 s and 41.5 s totals, the others missed and wrote 172-185 s. The whole 226 s gap between the two columns is a cache-hit artifact. The comparable quantity is hif4_dynamic_quantize_activation alone, which is timed per call in every shard under identical conditions, and that is what the time section uses.

controls.B_output_identity: parent and candidate agree byte for byte (raw .numpy().tobytes(), not torch.equal -- NaN != NaN under torch.equal) on: the compiled synthetic layer (16 steps, 2586 group moves, 2586 mantissa codes changed), a state with no em1 payload (both take the `no-metric` arm), the out-of-scope in_features=4160 bypass (both take the `out-of-scope` arm), and 128 real rows of the cached layer-0/q state (16 steps, 40167 group moves, 2044 rows kept, 40167 mantissa codes changed)
controls.C_gradient_identity: the two products of the pre-loop gradient are bit-identical to the two products of the pass-0 recomputation, on both the synthetic layer (shapes (12,2560)@(2560,2560) twice) and the real layer-0/q state ((128,2560)@(2560,2560) twice); product 0 identical true, product 1 identical true in both
controls.D_operator_accounting: the complete Tensor.mm sequence is recorded for both arms by wrapping torch.Tensor.mm. K=1: the parent issues 20 products and the candidate 18, and the candidate's shape sequence equals the parent's with products 2 and 3 removed and no other change. Verified on both the synthetic layer and the real layer-0/q state. This is the card's entire claim, measured rather than argued from reading the source
controls.E1_nonfinite_path: a NaN reference takes the parent's own `nonfinite-gradient` path in both arms, and both return the result untouched, byte for byte -- so the pre-loop finiteness check the parent performs is still performed and still decides the same way
controls.E2_later_pass_unchanged: at K=2 in memory only, the pass-1 gradient is poisoned with NaN at the mm call the parent would reach. The parent issues 22 products and aborts at index 21; the candidate issues 20 and aborts at index 19 -- exactly the 2-product offset, meaning both stopped before any second-pass group step -- and their outputs are byte-identical. This is the control that shows the guard did not lift the recomputation out of the loop: at K>=2 the later passes still recompute and still stop where the parent stops
controls.F_determinism_and_state: two consecutive calls bit-identical; torch.save/load of the state round-trips bit-identical; K=2 set in memory and restored to 1 leaves the shipped K=1 behaviour intact; accepted_steps=16 (cap 16) on both synthetic and real, i.e. one pass of the parent's 16-group schedule

reason: All 336 paired cases report a gain delta of exactly 0.0 (min 0.0, max 0.0; 0 positive, 0 negative). That exactness is not a tolerance claim: it is the evaluator's own paired statistic landing on zero everywhere, and behind it verify.py compares the raw output bytes field by field on the synthetic layer, the no-metric state, the out-of-scope bypass and 128 real rows. The change is proven to remove exactly two matrix products per call (20 -> 18 at K=1) and nothing else. What it is worth in wall-clock time could not be measured on this machine, with a sham null showing the estimator's own paired median drifting further than the effect; that is recorded as a limit of the measurement, not as a result.
